articles.title: FIFO vs weighted-average crypto cost basis: a worked ledger
articles.excerpt: Calculate proceeds, fees, realized profit and the remaining inventory without confusing a trading estimate with a tax return.
paragraphs: Why trade-level cost matters

A total portfolio gain does not tell you the cost of a specific disposal. Each purchase adds a quantity of tokens and a fee-inclusive purchase cost. Each sale produces net proceeds after its selling fee. Realized P&L compares net proceeds with the part of historical purchase cost allocated to the quantity sold. This arithmetic is consistent even when price quotes fluctuate.
FIFO example

Imagine buying 2 tokens at USD 100 each with a USD 2 fee, then 3 tokens at USD 120 each with a USD 3 fee. The first lot has a total cost of USD 202, or USD 101 per token. If you later sell one token for USD 150 and pay USD 1 selling fee, FIFO gives USD 149 net proceeds, USD 101 cost basis, and USD 48 realized profit. The remaining four tokens retain their own underlying purchase costs.
Weighted-average example

With the same five tokens purchased for a total of USD 565, the weighted-average cost is USD 113 per token. The same one-token sale at net proceeds of USD 149 produces USD 36 realized profit under this arithmetic method. The cash proceeds did not change; the allocated basis did. For this illustration, FIFO and weighted-average results differ by USD 12 because of their different cost allocation conventions.
Data workflow and limits

Import rows in chronological order, with distinct transaction IDs, asset ticker, BUY/SELL, quantity, USD price and USD fee. Reject a sale larger than the recorded holdings rather than silently allowing a short sale. This calculator assumes one USD quote currency, long-only positions, no coin transfers, no fork/airdrop adjustments and no tax-lot elections. Which method is legally appropriate depends on jurisdiction and records, so the figures are not a filing recommendation.
faq: Does a weighted-average result automatically qualify for tax filing?
No. This worksheet compares arithmetic inventory methods; applicable tax-lot rules depend on the jurisdiction and specific asset records.
Can one sale have different realized profit under different cost conventions?
Yes. The same net sale proceeds can be matched to different purchase-cost allocations, changing the computed realized gain.

articles.title: Time-weighted return vs XIRR: which performance number is different?
articles.excerpt: A reproducible example separates investment growth from cash deposits and explains two commonly confused performance measures.
paragraphs: The difference in purpose

Time-weighted return (TWR) aims to measure changes in portfolio value independently from the size and timing of outside cash deposits. XIRR is a money-weighted annualized rate that depends on the dated amounts of contributions and withdrawals. They often disagree for perfectly legitimate reasons. A single headline return does not reveal whether it includes new investor capital.
One worked TWR interval

Assume a portfolio opens at USD 1,000. After performance, but immediately before a USD 100 end-of-period deposit, its value is USD 1,050. At the period end, the recorded account value becomes USD 1,150. With the deposit treated as occurring at the end, the period return equals (1,150 − 100) / 1,000 − 1 = 5%, not 15%. Chain subsequent period factors to estimate total TWR.
One worked XIRR interval

An investment of USD 1,000 on January 1, 2026 and a withdrawal of USD 1,100 on January 1, 2027 have a 10% annualized XIRR under a 365-day year for this simple two-flow case. A midyear contribution alters the money-weighted result even when the asset price path is unchanged. The numerical root solves the sum of dated cash flows discounted by (1 + r) raised to the elapsed-year fractions.
Read the assumptions before trusting the result

The browser TWR worksheet assumes external contributions and withdrawals happen at the end of each valuation interval. Provide a valuation on each material cashflow day to limit distortion. The XIRR solver rejects cashflows with multiple sign changes, because such cases may have multiple mathematically valid roots. Neither number includes unrecorded market prices, custody losses or future investment performance.
sources: CFA Institute: Global Investment Performance Standards overview
faq: Does TWR subtract my contributions from growth?
It neutralizes outside money flows within the stated valuation-period timing assumption rather than treating deposits as investment profit.
Why is XIRR annualized?
It solves for a constant annualized discount rate that balances dated positive and negative cashflows; multiple roots can occur in nonstandard cases.

articles.title: Why a moving-average backtest must not trade on tomorrow's information
articles.excerpt: Work through previous-close trading signals, next-open simulated fills and costs with a transparent historical data example.
paragraphs: What look-ahead bias means

A historical strategy can appear impressive when a simulator accidentally lets it trade at a price that was not known until later. For example, computing a moving-average crossover from a day's closing price and then pretending the trade occurred at the beginning of that same day uses future information. The apparent success cannot be reproduced in real time using that rule.
One reproducible signal

Consider a simple moving average (SMA) over two recent closes and another over three recent closes. At the end of day 3, the observed closes are 10, 11 and 12 USD. The fast average is (11 + 12) / 2 = 11.5; the slow average is (10 + 11 + 12) / 3 = 11. If a strategy first permits purchases when the fast average exceeds the slow one, the earliest hypothetical execution based on those observations is day 4's opening price, not day 3's opening price.
What the scenario engine models

The CoinMetriq SMA teaching tool holds either cash or a long position. It uses prior-close data to decide each next-open buy or sale, applies the stated percentage fee to each simulated transaction, and revalues the position at that day's closing price. A companion buy-and-hold comparison uses the same initial cash and a simplified fee-inclusive entry. Both are hypothetical, deterministic and fully based on your imported historical OHLCV rows.
What it cannot infer

The tool does not simulate spread, live order-book liquidity, market impact, funding, tax, chain latency or exchange downtime. Selecting SMA lengths after seeing the historical results can itself overfit the sample. A larger or more sophisticated backtest is not proof that the strategy will work in unseen market conditions, and none of the results are a trade recommendation.
sources: Bitcoin historical market data is not embedded; use your own lawfully obtained CSV
faq: Why does the example strategy trade at the next open?
The strategy learns the completed moving averages only at the prior close, so using that day's earlier opening price would introduce future knowledge.
Do simulated transaction costs reflect live execution?
No. The model uses a manual percentage fee and excludes slippage, order-book depth, outages and latency.

articles.title: Crypto wallet permissions: spotting approval and recovery-phrase scams
articles.excerpt: Recognize suspicious token approval requests and recovery-phrase demands without ever connecting a wallet to this website.
paragraphs: Why a wallet connection is not a trust certificate

A wallet can display an account address or a pending signature request without proving that the requesting website is trustworthy. A familiar logo, a screenshot of a celebrity, or a supposed moderator's private message is not independent verification. Check the real project domain through an independently sourced channel rather than clicking links offered inside a surprise message.
Private keys and recovery phrases

A recovery phrase can grant access to wallet funds. A legitimate troubleshooting website does not need to receive your phrase to calculate a portfolio fee or explain blockchain concepts. CoinMetriq has no wallet connector and deliberately provides no field for secret phrases. Do not paste wallet keys, recovery phrases, exchange login credentials or personally sensitive records into any public research form.
Allowance and permit risk

On some token networks, a dapp may ask for permission to spend a token up to an allowance. The authorization can persist beyond the first transaction. A signature may authorize a later action even if the immediate page looks harmless. Before approving, inspect the target contract/network, the requested permission, the amount and the wallet's available transaction details. If unsure, stop.
Fictional warning-sign checklist

A marketing page guarantees extraordinary returns with zero risk, then asks for your recovery phrase to release an airdrop or demands an unusual unlock fee before a withdrawal. These are warning signs, not proof of any particular exchange's behavior. Use a securely bookmarked official source or trusted independent provider documentation to check claims. An educational checklist cannot certify a wallet or smart contract as safe.
sources: MetaMask token approval and signature phishing
faq: Does a hardware wallet make every approval safe?
No. It can protect key material while still signing an unsafe permission that a user approves.
Should I ever paste my recovery phrase into a support website?
No. A third party requesting it is a severe warning sign; use the wallet vendor's independently verified guidance.

articles.title: Bitcoin halving, block subsidy and transaction fees are three different concepts
articles.excerpt: A historical block-height timeline distinguishes new coin issuance, total miner reward and network transaction fees.
paragraphs: Block reward is made from two parts

A Bitcoin miner who successfully constructs a valid block may claim a block subsidy and the transaction fees associated with eligible included transactions. The block subsidy is newly issued bitcoin, while transaction fees are value transferred from users according to their transactions. Calling the entire miner reward newly minted bitcoin is therefore incorrect.
The four past subsidy changes

At block heights 210,000, 420,000, 630,000 and 840,000 the subsidy decreased from 50 to 25, 12.5, 6.25 and 3.125 BTC per block, respectively. These historical transitions occurred in 2012, 2016, 2020 and 2024. The 210,000-block schedule is defined by consensus rules, not by a promise that a new block must appear every ten minutes precisely.
Future dates and market prices

The next scheduled block-height threshold is a protocol calculation, not a fixed calendar date. Actual dates depend on the observed rate at which blocks are found and on network conditions. Bitcoin's supply rule is not a pricing model; historical halvings do not demonstrate that the USD price must rise by a specified multiplier on a future date.
How to use the timeline safely

The historical timeline labels a past subsidy transition and points readers to Bitcoin technical references. For any financial research based on a specific block event, independently verify chain history, UTC timestamps and current consensus implementation. Transaction fees and the full miner reward must be considered separately from the subsidy count.
faq: Does a halving reduce transaction fees by half?
No. The scheduled halving changes the new-coin block subsidy; users' transaction fees vary separately.
Can CoinMetriq predict the next halving date or Bitcoin price?
No. Calendar timing depends on observed blocks and future price depends on independent market forces.

articles.title: Why a network fee rate and a transaction fee are not the same number
articles.excerpt: Convert virtual bytes and a user-entered fee rate to satoshis, BTC and a hypothetical USD equivalent.
paragraphs: A calculation with labeled units

For a Bitcoin-like transaction, suppose a raw or virtual size estimate is 140 vbytes and the chosen hypothetical rate is 5 satoshis per vbyte. Multiplication produces 700 satoshis. Since one BTC has 100 million satoshis, this is 0.000007 BTC. If a manual BTC/USD reference were 80,000, the illustrative fiat equivalent would be USD 0.56. None of these example inputs is a recommended live rate.
A rate does not guarantee confirmation time

A fee rate expresses a bid for the scarce space in a block. The result depends on transaction structure and network policy, other users' demand and miner selection. A well-labeled fee estimator needs to distinguish vbytes from raw bytes and avoid treating its output as a guarantee of immediate inclusion.
What confirmations indicate

After a transaction enters a chain block, each subsequent block built on that block adds another confirmation according to common counting conventions. Confirmation count can be evidence of additional accumulated work, but it is not an absolute guarantee that the chain cannot reorganize. Different blockchains have different finality and fee models.
When your inputs are stale

CoinMetriq deliberately avoids a live mempool connection. If you enter a hypothetical rate from an old article, the arithmetic remains correct while the practical payment outcome may differ completely. For current fees, use reliable wallet/provider tooling and independently verify that you are transacting on the intended chain.
faq: What is one satoshi?
One satoshi is one hundred-millionth of a bitcoin; BTC amounts in this worksheet use that mathematical conversion.
Does a fee-rate estimate guarantee confirmation time?
No. Demand, network conditions, transaction structure and miner selection can change timing.

articles.title: Staking APR vs APY: what a compounding example actually shows
articles.excerpt: Turn a nominal staking rate into a mathematical compounding scenario without inventing yield or market guarantees.
paragraphs: APR and effective APY differ

A nominal annual percentage rate describes an annual rate without necessarily accounting for reinvestment frequency. An effective compounded annual percentage yield (APY), in a simplified deterministic scenario, equals (1 + APR / periods)^periods − 1, with APR expressed as a fraction. If rewards are not actually reinvested, this textbook formula is not the realized return.
A clear scenario with numbers

Assume 100 example tokens, a stated nominal 12% APR, and monthly compounding over one year. The final quantity is 100 × (1 + 0.12/12)^12, approximately 112.6825 tokens. The extra 12.6825 tokens exceed a simple noncompounded 12-token result because the model reinvests each monthly reward. The formula is an assumption, not a current provider quotation.
What real staking may introduce

Network validation can include variable rewards, slashing, penalties, lockups, custody risk and the difference between liquid receipt tokens and underlying token holdings. Market price may decline even while the token count rises. Taxes and fees may further reduce realizable returns. Carefully inspect the rules of the actual chain and chosen custodian.
Using the calculator

Enter starting token quantity, a hypothetical nominal APR, periods of compounding per year and duration in years. The browser returns the modeled token increase and effective annual rate. Treat every input as a scenario until validated against current provider terms, since the tool intentionally fetches no live APY feed.
faq: What makes APY differ from APR?
The simplified APY example assumes rewards are added back to principal at a selected frequency; nominal APR does not itself describe such reinvestment.
Can token count rise while USD investment value falls?
Yes. A decline in the market price may outweigh a hypothetical increase in token quantity.

articles.title: Constant-product AMM impermanent loss: an example without hype
articles.excerpt: Calculate a theoretical 50/50 pool's relative outcome versus holding the tokens, excluding fees and platform risks.
paragraphs: What is being compared?

For a simplified 50/50 constant-product liquidity pool, the classical impermanent-loss expression compares the pool position value to holding the same starting tokens outside the pool after a relative price change. The expression is 2 × square-root(price ratio) / (1 + price ratio) − 1. It does not include fee income, incentive rewards or changes in protocol operation.
A two-to-one price example

If the price ratio rises from 1 to 2, the expression becomes 2 × √2 / 3 − 1, approximately −5.7191%. This negative percentage represents the theoretical shortfall relative to simply holding the original tokens. It does not state that the pool position's value fell by 5.7191% in dollar terms. Pool returns can still be positive or negative against different benchmarks.
The simplifying conditions

This equation is specific to the simple constant-product, 50/50 pool setup. Concentrated liquidity, unequal asset weights, changes in peg behavior, accrued trading fees, incentive distributions and protocol exploits alter the result. Readers should not apply the shortcut indiscriminately to every token pool.
Test with your own assumptions

Our calculator accepts only a positive new-to-old price ratio and shows the mathematical relative effect. To compare a real liquidity provider position, you would also need position boundaries, fees, token reserves, rewards and protocol-specific conditions. No historical price series or live pool state is fetched.
faq: Is the quoted impermanent loss the total dollar loss?
No. It compares a modelled pool position with a hold-only benchmark; fees and price movements require additional accounting.
Does the 50/50 formula describe concentrated liquidity pools?
No. Concentrated liquidity, custom weights and other pool designs have different conditions and mathematics.

articles.title: Dollar-cost averaging vs lump sum in crypto: same budget, different timing
articles.excerpt: A reproducible four-period comparison shows why DCA can win or lose depending on price path, without promising future performance.
paragraphs: First establish an equal budget

Lump-sum buying and dollar-cost averaging (DCA) are different cash-deployment schedules. A fair mathematical comparison uses the same total starting budget and the same eventual valuation date, otherwise a return difference may reflect different invested amounts rather than timing. DCA buys a fixed cash amount across periods; it usually acquires more token units when the token price is lower and fewer when it is higher.
Exact four-period example

Assume four fictional observed prices of USD 100, USD 80, USD 120 and USD 90, a total budget of USD 400, and a later illustrative final reference price of USD 110. Investing all USD 400 at the first price buys 4 units, worth USD 440 at the example final price. Splitting the budget into four equal USD 100 purchases acquires 1 + 1.25 + 0.833333 + 1.111111 = approximately 4.194444 units. At USD 110, their modeled value is approximately USD 461.39, or USD 21.39 higher than the lump-sum value.
Why the answer can reverse

DCA is not universally better. If a token rose in a steady sequence after the first date, the first-price lump sum could obtain more units than the later purchases. Conversely, an early price drop can benefit staged buying. The comparison tool uses only your supplied sequence and provides the unit and value difference; it does not estimate the probability of future price directions, appropriate investment timing or personal risk tolerance.
Fees, interest and honest assumptions

This simplified example leaves out exchange spreads, percentage and flat trading fees, bank transfer costs, idle cash interest, custody risk and investment taxes. If the same total budget is deployed on different dates, the cash left uninvested during the DCA period should also be documented in a fuller total-return calculation. Use sample CSV or manually entered price observations; CoinMetriq never fetches a live price or recommends a trading schedule.
faq: Does a lower average price always make DCA the winner?
No. The end value depends on total token units, identical total funding, price path and transaction costs.
Is this an automatic investment plan?
No. It is a browser-only educational comparison using manually entered hypothetical prices.

articles.title: Crypto price impact, slippage and exchange fees: three separate costs
articles.excerpt: Learn how a small quoted price impact and percentage exchange fee produce an exact hypothetical fill cost on a USD 1,000 purchase.
paragraphs: Distinguish the terms before adding percentages

Quoted mid-price, order execution price, price impact and transaction fees answer different questions. A trade can change the marginal price available from a liquidity pool because of its size, while slippage can reflect a difference between expected and realized execution. A swap interface may also present a separate explicit platform or pool fee. Double-counting an interface's quoted impact and its realized execution difference would make a cost estimate unreliable.
A fully labeled numerical example

Suppose a fictional quoted unit price is USD 100 and a purchaser wants ten units. The reference notional is USD 1,000. Model a 0.5% unfavorable execution slippage for a purchase, then a separate 0.1% exchange fee applied to the executed notional. The execution notional is USD 1,005 and the explicit fee is USD 1.005. The all-in modeled cost is USD 1,006.005, which is USD 6.005 above the starting quote. The effective cost per unit is USD 100.6005.
Price impact and slippage are not interchangeable

In a constant-product automated market maker, a sufficiently large trade moves along the pool's pricing curve. Slippage instead compares an expected output or rate with what the trade finally executes at. The two may interact, and a user-interface's minimum output tolerance is not a fixed fee. Actual fills can be rejected, partially filled or worse than a displayed quote within platform rules; a calculator cannot certify live execution.
What this browser worksheet leaves out

The scenario intentionally uses a manual unfavorable slippage rate and an explicit percentage fee, compounded on the execution notional. It does not fetch order books, reserves, chain gas, oracle prices, local taxes or the exact settlement price for a particular exchange. Compare input timestamps and currencies before using the result for research. This is not a swap interface or trading recommendation.
faq: Is the displayed price impact itself a fee?
No. Price impact describes how trade size changes the available rate; explicit network and exchange charges must be considered separately.
Can I treat this as a live Uniswap quote?
No. The worksheet has no network connection and accepts fictional or user-entered price, slippage and fee inputs.
sources: Uniswap Labs: Price Impact vs Price Slippage
